t: For necessary expenses for overseas construction and related costs, and for the procurement and enhancement of information technology and related capital investments, pursuant to section 667 of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, $174,985,000, to remain available until expended:  Provided, That this amount is in addition to funds otherwise available for such purposes:  Provided further, That funds appropriated under this heading shall be available subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.

fable.w: This is an appropriation for overseas construction and information technology capital investments. The tempting reading is that the "notification procedures" clause counts as a consultative process, but the notification goes to the Committees on Appropriations, which are part of Congress and therefore inside the federal government. No state, tribe, company, expert, or member of the public is involved in any federal decision here.
fable.s: funds appropriated under this heading shall be available subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations

qwen_block.w: The section requires notification to the Committees on Appropriations, which are part of Congress. Congress is inside the federal government, so this is intra-governmental coordination, not participation by outside parties. The text does not mention consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: funds appropriated under this heading shall be available subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.

opus.w: This is an appropriation for overseas construction and information technology. The only procedure it mentions is notifying the congressional Appropriations Committees, and those committees are inside the federal government. There is no public comment, outside advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or right to sue, so the notification requirement does not count as participation.
opus.s: funds appropriated under this heading shall be available subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations
opus.b: Step 1. The tempting wrong reading is that "regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations" counts as participation because it is a formal procedure. It fails because the Committees on Appropriations are part of Congress, which is inside the federal government. Nobody outside the federal government is involved in any decision here.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires notification to the Committees on Appropriations. Under the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Notification to an internal government body does not constitute participation with people outside the government.
qwen_chat.s: Provided further, That funds appropriated under this heading shall be available subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations" involves coordination with an outside entity. However, Congress and its committees are explicitly defined as INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, reporting to or notifying Congress is intra-governmental communication, not participation with outsiders.
